Article Title: Congress takes 'Kya hua tera vada' dig at govt over 'skyrocketing' prices of food items
Article Text:
Congress targets PM Modi, Centre over rising food prices, inflation.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led central government over "skyrocketing prices" of food and other commodities, using the popular Bollywood song "Kya hua tera vada" to question the PM's silence on inflation.Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on rising prices of food items, pulses and cooking oil, and alleged that the increase was putting pressure on household budgets."The skyrocketing prices of food items in the country have broken the back of the middle and poor classes," Ramesh said in a post in Hindi. He said rising prices were making pulses and other essential food items increasingly difficult for poorer households to afford."But the Prime Minister remains silent on inflation. The country is asking, 'Where have the 'achche din' gone, Prime Minister ji?' Are they only left in sermons?" he said."The people go hungry, the government stays silent," Ramesh said, questioning whether this was the "new India".Taking a swipe at the government, Ramesh wrote, "Kya hua tera vada? Woh kasam, woh irada?", a reference to the popular song from the 1977 Bollywood film Hum Kisise Kum Nahin.Ramesh claimed that prices of several everyday commodities had risen sharply in recent months, adding to the burden on households."In the past month, spice prices have surged by a massive 10% to 25%. Green cardamom has risen from 4000 rupees to 4400 rupees/kg, black cardamom from 2400 rupees to 2800 rupees/kg, and cumin has jumped from 360 rupees to 400 rupees/kg. Mace prices have shot up directly from 2500 rupees to 3000 rupees per kg,” Jairam said."Arhar dal has increased from 100 rupees to 130 rupees/kg, chana dal from 70 rupees to 100 rupees/kg, and urad from 120 rupees to 140 rupees/kg. Mustard oil has reached 210 rupees/litre from 190 rupees, and Safola oil has climbed to 280 rupees/litre from 240 rupees," he added.Ramesh also claimed that onion prices had risen sharply between June and September. “From June to September, the all-India average retail price of onions rose from 29.50 rupees/kg to 53.78 rupees/kg - a staggering 82.3% increase in just three and a half months," he said.The Congress leader called on the Modi government to take immediate measures to address what he described as "uncontrolled inflation" and provide relief to consumers.
Article Summary: Congress targets pm modi, centre over rising food prices, inflation. Congress general secretary in-charge communications jairam ramesh shared a media report on rising prices of food items, pulses and cooking oil. He said rising prices were making pulses and other essential food items increasingly difficult for poorer households to afford.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Indian Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh and Japan Air Self-Defence Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita took sorties on Tejas fighter aircraft on Sunday.This comes amid the ongoing Indo-Japan bilateral air exercise 'Veer Guardian-2026' at Air Force Station Jodhpur in Rajasthan.The IAF is participating with a mix of frontline combat aircraft, including the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale fighter jets, while the JASDF has deployed its F-2A fighter aircraft.The exercise, which began on September 9 and will continue till September 22, involves advanced operational missions, mission planning and professional exchanges between personnel of the two air forces.The participation of Japanese fighter aircraft in the exercise marks the first time JASDF combat aircraft have operated from Indian soil.Earlier, on September 10, defence minister Rajnath Singh described Japan sending its fighter aircraft to participate in Exercise Veer Guardian as a "significant milestone" for the India-Japan defence partnership.In a post on X, he said the maiden visit of Japan Air Self-Defence Force fighter aircraft to India reflected growing trust and a shared commitment to peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.He also recalled his "highly productive discussions" with his Japanese counterpart in New Delhi last month, saying exchanges such as Exercise Veer Guardian would further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.The Indian Air Force had welcomed the Japanese F-2 fighter jets to Jodhpur on September 8 ahead of the exercise. During the 14-day drill, air warriors from the two countries are undertaking advanced operational missions and engaging in extensive professional interactions.
Article Summary: Indian air chief marshal amar preet singh and japan air self-defence force chief of staff general takehiro morita took sorties on tejas fighter aircraft on sunday. Article Title: Muslim clerics distance themselves from Hamid Ansari's ‘Hindu extremism’ remarks; call for harmony
Article Text:
‘We are proud we live in India’: Imam body chief hits back at Hamid Ansari over ‘Hindu extremism’ remarks.

The remarks by former Vice President Hamid Ansari on “Hindu extremism” and the RSS have drawn criticism from Muslim clerics, with All India Imam Association president Maulana Sajid Rashidi saying Muslims should not be made to feel like outsiders in India.Rashidi said people who hold constitutional posts are expected to represent all sections of society and questioned Ansari's decision to speak on such issues after leaving office.Speaking to ANI, Rashidi said Ansari had not made many statements in favour of Muslims while serving as Vice President but had spoken on several such issues after leaving office."Hamid Ansari sahab, when he was Vice President, you did not see many statements from him in favour of Muslims. But after leaving that post, several statements have come from him, and it appears as if he is now presenting himself as a leader of Muslims."Rashidi also said extremism should be judged by whether it promotes hatred against other communities."Extremism becomes wrong when hatred against others comes into it. If someone follows their religion and does not trouble others, that is a different matter," he said.'We are even prouder that we live in India'Rashidi said Muslims had chosen to remain in India during Partition and had contributed to the country."We say with pride that we are Muslims, but we are even prouder that we live in India," he said.He said remarks suggesting that Muslims do not belong in India could create a sense of insecurity within the community. He called on political organisations and leaders to act against statements targeting any community.Rashidi also referred to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's remarks on Hindu-Muslim relations and said calls for communal harmony should be followed by people across communities.Earlier on Sunday, chief Imam of All India Imam Organisation Umer Ahmed Ilyasi also criticised Ansari over his comments on "Hindu extremism".Ilyasi alleged that Ansari's remarks were intended to provoke Muslims and could disturb the social atmosphere."I strongly condemn this statement. Today, Hamid Ansari sahab has remembered Muslims again. When he was in power and held important positions, he was secular. Today, he has remembered Muslims.Ilyasi further alleged that Ansari was trying to regain his standing among Muslims and claimed that his remarks could create tension in society."Muslims are not asking about him, and to improve his image among Muslims, he has made such statements. I feel that somewhere this is a big conspiracy to disturb the atmosphere of the country," Ilyasi said.
Article Summary: ‘we are proud we live in india’: imam body chief hits back at hamid ansari over ‘hindu extremism’ remarks. All india imam association president maulana sajid rashidi says muslims should not be made to feel like outsiders in india.

NEW DELHI: The death toll from the attack on the police lines headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rose to at least 31, with over 100 injured, as military and police forces concluded the 22-hour-long stand-off Saturday noon.What began on Friday as a suicide blast at the compound's perimeter gate rapidly developed into an active siege after at least seven operatives from the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP) group breached the counter terrorism department (CTD) and intelligence facilities. In a turn of events, the operatives, once inside, managed to reach the facility's weapons depot, released many detained terror suspects, and armed some of them to fight the Pakistani personnel, sources said.Despite a large deployment, heavy gunfire was exchanged through Friday night and Saturday morning. A military command with the infantry division was used to direct the Pak govt's operation, but strong resistance from inside the lockdown zone prolonged the multi-building standoff, leaving scores wounded and critical.Among those killed were SP Akbar Shinwari, a deputy SP and Dr Israel Orakzai, head of the pediatrics department at Kohat hospital.A few civilians also died in the exchange of fire.Special Service Group (SSG) Zarrar unit and infantry division had to be pressed into service to end the siege and clear the compound. Khyber Police claimed to have neutralised eight of the attackers. The facility, which has been facilitating establishment of new terror camps in KPK region, was struck Friday afternoon with a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED), enabling multiple suicide attackers to force their way inside the premises shooting indiscriminately.

Article Title: SC 'banyan tree' of environmental justice: CJI Surya Kant
Article Text:
Environmental issues have no geographical limitations, said CJI Surya Kant

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the right to a pollution-free environment be considered a fundamental right? Yes, absolutely No, not necessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Terming Supreme Court the "banyan tree" of environmental justice for its role in protecting the environment and ecology, CJI Surya Kant Saturday said conservation and development are not in conflict with each other and there is need to maintain balance between them.Addressing the inaugural session of 'The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics' organised by NGT, he said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom to sprout into life and SC has played that role."And it is here that SC has stood tall as the banyan tree of environmental justice, with roots deep in our civilisational ethos and branches sheltering the rights of unseen generations. It has over the decades championed the idea that progress without preservation is but a mirage that vanishes in the desert of ecological ruin. Its rulings underscore how safeguarding nature is not an act of altruism but of self-preservation, an investment in the very continuity of life. "Highlighting its proactive approach, he said SC has made the right to a pollution-free environment a fundamental right by reading it directly into Article 21 ."That same pattern has carried us to the present day, where SC recently articulated the idea of 'eco-centric proportionality', postulating that environmental protection must be rigorous yet intelligent enough to engage with the world as it exists. This notion has advanced the most pragmatic approach of permitting development solely in conjunction with enforceable conditions, expert oversight, restoration, compensatory afforestation and accountability."Recent Indian jurisprudence on climate has brought this question into sharper constitutional focus by recognising the adverse effects of climate change can impact fundamental rights of equality, livelihood, health and conditions necessary for meaningful enjoyment of these rights," he added.
Article Summary: Environmental issues have no geographical limitations, said cji surya kant. He said there are constitutional provisions for protection of environment, but words in a constitution are only seeds which need the nurturing waters of judicial wisdom to sprout into life.

Article Title: PM Modi pushes back on West’s narrative over carbon emissions
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi Saturday questioned the narrative in which the responsibility for carbon emissions is pinned on developing countries while Western countries are absolved of their role as historical polluters, even as he reaffirmed the country’s commitment to climate action and stressed that it has the best record among G20 countries. “In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s... India presents this fact strongly on global platforms... We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” he said. His remarks at an international conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, organised by NGT, come as the world gears up for the global climate conference scheduled for Nov in Turkiye.He said India is providing solutions to modern climate challenges even as its per capita carbon emissions are less than half of the global average.The PM’s remarks are being seen as a pushback against the West’s attempt, despite its historical responsibility for alarming emission levels, to suggest that India needs to accept stiff emission-reduction targets. India’s cumulative (1751-2024) contribution to overall carbon emissions is merely 3.5%, compared with 23.5% for US, 15.4% for China, 6.6% for Russia, 5.1% for Germany, and 4.3% for UK.Though India is currently the third-largest emitter, its per capita emission, as Modi underlined, at 2.2 tonnes per person per year, is less than half of the global average (4.7 tonnes per person per year) and six times less than the per capita emission of US (14.2 tonnes) and Russia (14 tonnes).India has always raised these points at all multilateral forums, pointing to equity and importance of a cut in emissions by big polluters who developed by burning fossil fuels over the past two centuries, which led to global warming. India, however, has never deviated from its responsibility and has fulfilled climate action pledges under the Paris Agreement.“India is the only country in G20 that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP21 summit in Paris (in 2015), and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of ‘Hindustan’ that I am talking about. On every parameter — non-fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions — India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide,” said PM Modi while urging the gathering of jurists, academicians, policymakers, scientists, environmental experts and other stakeholders from 17 countries across the world to look at the figures.Looking ahead to COP31, scheduled for Nov in Antalya, Turkey, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav said India will continue to advocate climate action centred on equity, implementation and the needs of vulnerable countries.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi questioned the narrative in which the responsibility for carbon emissions is pinned on developing countries. He said india is providing solutions to modern climate challenges even as its per capita carbon emissions are less than half of the global average.

Article Title: Targets approved, bombs loaded & then Trump blinked: Why US pulled back from Houthi strikes
Article Text:
File photo: US President Donald Trump with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman

Why is Trump hesitating

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the decision to halt the airstrikes against the Houthis in Yemen? Yes, it was a wise decision. No, action needed to be taken. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

US President Donald Trump had moved to launch airstrikes against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) pressed him to intervene. But Trump abruptly halted the operation before the strikes could begin.A report by New York Times states that Trump had spent nearly two weeks wavering over whether to join Saudi Arabia in its renewed fight against the Houthis. On Wednesday, he told advisers he did not favour strikes. But after MBS called him on Thursday and again urged US military help, Trump reversed course and instructed the Pentagon to prepare airstrikes.According to two people briefed on the attack, Pentagon commanders had created approved target lists, troops were loading bombs onto warplanes selected for the missions and US military was prepared for fresh attacks on the Iranian proxy group. the wave of attacks was just about to begin.But by Sunday, however, Trump had reversed his decision yet again. The strikes were put on hold, at least for now, even as preparations for the attack had advanced significantly. The White House declined to discuss Trump's deliberations, while a senior administration official said only that the US had a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and would defend its allies.The sudden U-turn reflects a larger problem for Trump. The Houthis have avoided attacking US ships and have agreed, for now, not to fight the United States.But they have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, leaving Trump under pressure from a key ally that Washington also needs in its wider war against Iran.Saudi Arabia has shown it can use that dependence as leverage. In May, Riyadh effectively blocked a US plan to use American forces to escort commercial oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz by denying US forces access to its airspace and military bases.The Houthi threat has also expanded beyond Saudi Arabia. The group has attacked Saudi vessels and declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea, while capturing areas near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a crucial maritime chokepoint. The developments have raised fresh concerns over global shipping and energy supplies.A new US bombing campaign would risk opening another front while American forces are already stretched by the war against Iran. Several officials and commanders have also questioned whether airstrikes would force the Houthis to back down.The US spent more than 50 days bombing the group in 2025, striking over 1,000 targets and burning through about $1 billion in weapons and ammunition in the first month. Trump later called a ceasefire, saying the Houthis had promised to stop attacking ships.The Houthis have since rebuilt much of their military capability and are now using artificial intelligence to develop and engineer new missile systems, according to US officials. A renewed US campaign could also prompt the group to resume attacks on American ships and further disrupt shipping through the Bab al-Mandab, adding another pressure point to already unstable energy routes.Trump said Sunday that he remained in “deciding mode” over the larger Iran war. For now, however, the president has stepped back from striking the Houthis, despite having taken the US military to the brink of doing so.
Article Summary: Us president donald trump had moved to launch airstrikes against iran-backed houthis in yemen after saudi crown prince mohammed bin salman (mbs) pressed him to intervene. But trump abruptly halted the operation before the strikes could begin. The houthis have avoided attacking us ships and have agreed, for now, not to fight the united states.

Article Title: Pakistan airstrikes on Afghanistan: 3 killed, several injured as conflict fears grow
Article Text:
Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along border. (AP photo/ File)

Taliban warns of 'crushing response'

Kabul denies sheltering TTP

Afghanistan keeps door open for talks

At least three people were killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike targeting Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province, Tolo News reported on Monday, citing a provincial official.The military strike is supposedly in retaliation for suicide bombing at a police station compound in northwestern Pakistan, raising fears that tensions between the neighbouring nations could once again turn into open fighting.Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action.Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, ahead of the imminent Pakistani strikes, had warned Islamabad against carrying out strikes inside Afghanistan, saying Kabul would respond militarily if its territory is attacked.In an interview with Al Arabiya English, Mujahid rejected Pakistan's allegations that militant groups based in Afghanistan recruit, train and launch attacks against Pakistan.“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” Mujahid said.He said any Pakistani military operation inside Afghanistan would amount to a violation of Afghan sovereignty and could trigger a strong response from Kabul.Mujahid was responding to comments by a Pakistani military spokesperson, who had told Al Arabiya English that militant groups were using Afghan territory to recruit, train and arm fighters before sending them into Pakistan.Mujahid rejected those allegations and said the Taliban administration does not allow the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , or TTP, to operate from Afghan soil.He also denied that the Taliban government supports armed groups carrying out attacks against other countries. Instead, Mujahid said Pakistan should examine its own internal security problems, arguing that violence involving the TTP and Baloch armed groups existed before the Taliban returned to power in 2021.Pakistan has repeatedly accused militant groups of operating from Afghanistan and has pressed Kabul to take action against them. The Taliban has consistently denied allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.Despite his warning of military retaliation, Mujahid said Kabul was still willing to engage with Islamabad through dialogue.He called for stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements and greater bilateral cooperation to address security concerns along the two countries' border.Mujahid also backed a possible mediation role for Saudi Arabia, saying Riyadh has good relations with both Afghanistan and Pakistan and could help the two sides resolve their differences.Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border. The latest airstrike, coming amid fresh security concerns, risks further worsening those ties and could lead to another confrontation between the neighbours.
Article Summary: Relations between kabul and islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along border. The latest escalation comes days after the taliban warned that it would defend afghan territory against any pakistani military action. The taliban has consistently denied allowing afghan territory to be used for attacks against pakistan.

Days before Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's planned September 27 protest march, former prime minister Imran Khan 's son Kasim Khan has alleged that several members of his extended family have been detained and that their whereabouts have not been disclosed.In a series of posts on X, Kasim alleged that his aunts Dr Uzma and Noreen, along with cousins Shershah and Shahrez, were taken from their homes after authorities allegedly entered the properties and forced them into vehicles. The claims could not be independently verified.“This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noureen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez have now been abducted as well,” Kasim said.“They have broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated. No news has been released as to where they have been taken,” he alleged.Kasim described the alleged detentions as “criminal behaviour” and called for international attention to the matter.Kasim later said the two children of Shahrez, aged four and six, had initially been missing. Article Title: India-Japan air exercise Veer Guardian signals growing strategic alignment in the Indo-Pacific
Article Text:
JASDF Chief of Staff Masahiro Morita and IAF Chief of Air Staff AP Singh at Jodhpur Air Force Base during Ex Veer Guardian. (Image credit: IAF)

The successful conclusion of Exercise Veer Guardian 2026 has once again put the spotlight on just how far the India-Japan defence relationship has come, evolving from routine military exchanges into a genuinely comprehensive strategic partnership spanning operational cooperation, defence technology, maritime security and emerging military capabilities.This latest edition carried added weight because Japanese fighter aircraft operated from Indian soil for the very first time, a genuine milestone in the growing military engagement between the Indian Air Force and the Japan Air Self-Defense Force. Beyond the air combat drills, the exercise served as a visible demonstration of the trust, interoperability and strategic convergence steadily building between two of the Indo-Pacific's most important powers, both of whom share overlapping concerns about regional security.JASDF Chief General Takehiro Morita flew a sortie in a twin-seat variant of India's indigenous Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, calling it a symbol of India's technological innovation, a clear signal of Japan's appreciation for the country's growing aerospace capabilities. IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, for his part, led a Tejas formation flight during the exercise, underscoring both his own confidence in the indigenous platform and just how operationally mature the aircraft has become.For New Delhi and Tokyo, Veer Guardian represents far more than an air force engagement, it's one visible piece of a defence relationship that has expanded considerably over the past decade. Air Chief Marshal Singh's description of Japan as an "Apatsu Mitram," a friend in times of crisis, captured the level of strategic trust now underpinning bilateral ties. Both nations are Quad members, sharing a commitment to a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific, an outlook that has steadily translated into deeper cooperation across all three services. Apart from Veer Guardian, the armies of the two nations conduct Exercise Dharma Guardian, while the navies regularly engage through JAIMEX and the multilateral MILAN exercise.This growing military relationship rests on a series of agreements signed, covering defence cooperation and exchanges, equipment and technology transfers, protection of classified military information, and a Reciprocal Provision of Supplies and Services agreement, all of which have collectively enabled smoother logistics support and interoperability.Defence technology cooperation has also gained real momentum, with the two countries signing their first joint defence equipment project in 2024 an agreement to co-develop the UNICORN mast system for the Indian Navy's warships. The mast integrates radar and communication antennas into a single structure that reduces a warship's radar signature while improving efficiency, thus making the vessel a more effective combatant.Japan's transport aircraft and maritime patrol platforms an be another area of common interest for India. This opens up genuine opportunities for co-development and co-production under the Make in India framework, potentially letting Japanese firms tap into India's manufacturing ecosystem for both domestic and export markets.The recent visit of Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi added further weight to this trajectory. In talks with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, the two sides signed a Memorandum of Arrangement on maritime security cooperation, focused on maritime domain awareness, information sharing, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. Discussions also touched on mine countermeasures, shipbuilding, reciprocal ship repair facilities and joint defence research.The dialogue has even extended into next-generation technologies, with India examining pathways for future combat aviation capabilities, and reports suggesting discussions around potential Indian participation in Japan's Global Combat Air Programme, its sixth-generation fighter initiative. This programme is still at the exploratory stage and India is also in talks with France over the Future Combat Air System platform.Exercise Veer Guardian stands as a clear marker of a partnership that is increasingly operational, technology-driven and strategically significant. As both India and Japan deepen military cooperation amid a shifting Indo-Pacific security landscape.
Article Summary: The successful conclusion of exercise veer guardian 2026 has once again put the spotlight on just how far the india-japan defence relationship has come. The exercise served as a visible demonstration of the trust, interoperability and strategic convergence steadily building between two of the indo-pacific's most important powers.

Article Title: Planning a trip to Canada: Immigration agency answers the visa questions travellers often get wrong
Article Text:
Canada’s immigration agency answered some common questions

How long will a visitor visa actually take?

What documents do you need?

Can you work or study while visiting?

Read IRCC complete post here

Millions of people visit Canada every year. Here are some of the top questions about visiting Canada, answered!

1. Do I need a visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to travel to Canada?

To visit Canada, most people need a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA), depending on their citizenship, their travel document and the way they plan to travel to Canada.

Check if you need a visa or an eTA.

2. How long does it take to get a visitor visa?

If you need a visitor visa, you must complete an application and provide the required documents, which may include documents proving your identity, travel plans and eligibility to enter Canada. Processing times vary, so check the latest estimated processing time before you apply.

3. What documents do I need to apply for a visitor visa?

Your application needs to include a digital copy of your passport or travel document, which should be valid (not expired) for at least 6 months from the date you plan to travel.

When you apply online, you’ll get a personalized document checklist in the portal. Make sure you provide all the required documents.

4. Can I work or study while visiting Canada?

Visitors cannot work or study in Canada unless they’re authorized to do so. If you want to work or study here, you may also need a work permit or study permit.

Canada’s immigration authority has stepped in to clear up some of the most common confusion facing travellers. IRCC shared a post of social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) publishing a set of answers to the questions it says that visitors ask most often and the responses are worth a read before you book that trip. With millions of people visiting Canada every year, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) says a handful of questions come up again and again. Here's what the agency wants every prospective visitor to know.This is where many travellers get caught out. If you do need a visitor visa, you'll have to submit an application along with supporting documents proving your identity, travel plans, and eligibility to enter Canada — and processing times can vary significantly depending on demand and your location. IRCC is urging applicants to check current estimated processing times before applying, rather than assuming last year's timeline still holds.At a minimum, your application needs a digital copy of your passport or travel document, and it must remain valid for at least six months beyond your planned travel date — a detail that trips up more travellers than you'd expect. The good news: applying online generates a personalised document checklist inside the portal, so you know exactly what's required for your specific case rather than guessing.Here's the one that catches people out the most. Visitors are not permitted to work or study in Canada unless they're specifically authorized to do so. If your trip involves any work or study plans, a standard visitor visa or eTA won't cut it — you'll likely need a separate work permit or study permit, and IRCC recommends checking eligibility for either well before you travel.
Article Summary: Canada’s immigration agency answered some common questions about visiting the country. To visit canada, most people need a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eta) if you want to work or study here, you may also need a work permit or study permit.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: Jpmorgan chase ceo jamie dimon warns iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in ukraine, tensions in the middle east and friction with china. Dimon criticised revised us capital rules, including basel iii and gsib surcharge norms.

Article Title: How selling Alaska in 1867 was a costly mistake for Russia
Article Text:
Image: Wikipedia

Why Russia agreed to the Alaska purchase

The hidden wealth Russia gave away

Strategic and geopolitical consequences

In 1867, Russia’s decision to sell Alaska to America turned out to be a historic mistake that was to go unnoticed for years to come. The sum paid by the US was only $7,200,000. Although, in the light of the circumstances at the time, it appeared logical, retrospectively, the act looks extremely shortsighted. Russia found itself economically constrained, geographically far away from the region and fearful of its falling into the hands of the British without any compensation. In reality, however, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the United States.The choice of selling Alaska was based on economic and political reasons. By the middle of the 19th century, the Russian Empire experienced financial difficulties as a result of the expensive Crimean War. It had become increasingly hard for the country to manage such remote and thinly populated areas as Alaska.According to EBSCO , “the Russian-American Company was in decline, and the colony failed to yield any profit”.In addition to this, the lucrative fur trade had declined, making the territory much less economically valuable for the empire.At the same time, Russia was afraid that Britain might capture Alaska in case another war broke out between the two countries. Selling the colony to the friendly United States appeared as a logical step. As the Office of the Historian states, William H. Seward, U.S. Secretary of State, “it was a chance to expand its influence in North America and hinder further growth of Britain”.For Russia, the transaction was a chance to minimise the losses. However, it greatly undervalued the potential of Alaska.Another thing that Russia did not expect was the amount of riches that Alaska possessed. Within several decades after the acquisition, the state saw discoveries of enormous deposits of gold, oil, and other minerals.“Alaska has produced more than 40 million ounces of gold,” according to the US Geological Survey. Furthermore, Alaska is home to some of the world's most significant undeveloped mineral deposits, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) . But even more importantly, the state's oil deposits turned out to be extremely valuable. The Prudhoe Bay oil field was discovered in 1968 and became one of North America's biggest.In retrospect, the amount paid by the Americans, $7.2 million, or two cents per acre, was rather laughable. According to Howard I. Kushner , the deal “robbed Russia of an enormously rich territory, the true value of which would only be recognised in the twentieth century.”In addition to resources, there is the question of strategy and how important Alaska is to the United States from a strategic standpoint. This is a very good place when it comes to defence strategy. It borders on the Arctic Ocean and also happens to be close to Russia.During the period of the Cold War, the Alaskan region became a frontier area for the United States, becoming home to military facilities and warning systems.According to Col. Michael J. Forsyth, U.S. Army, the closeness of Russia and Alaska, only about ninety kilometres apart across the Bering Strait, meant that this region became highly significant to the United States' defence plans.From today's point of view, the strategic location of Alaska makes the state very important to the policies of the U.S. related to the Arctic, energy security, and even environmental policies.Thinking back, what seems clear to us now is that the Russians sold Alaska due to immediate needs rather than future considerations. In order to solve the problem, they lost a valuable resource for Russia.Conclusively, the Alaska Purchase should not have been done as it has had a significant impact that will remain throughout history.
Article Summary: In 1867, russia sold alaska to the united states for only $7,200,000. However, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the u.s.

Article Title: Ohio flash-flood threat persists as tornado warning ends
Article Text:
Vehicle in Ohio drives through floodwater at intersection. (Photo: Muskingam County Engineer's Office via Anadolu Agency via Reuters)

Storm warning carries 97kmph gusts

Up to 8.9cm rain recorded

A flash-flood warning remained in force across parts of southeastern Ohio into Monday morning after a tornado warning was cancelled late Sunday as severe weather continued across the region.At 11.13pm local time, the National Weather Service (NWS) issued a severe thunderstorm warning for eastern Vinton County and parts of southwestern Athens, northwestern Meigs, northeastern Gallia and northeastern Jackson counties. Radar indicated wind gusts of about 97kmph, while forecasters said a tornado remained possible.One minute later, the NWS cancelled the tornado warning for east-central Vinton and west-central Athens counties after the storm weakened below severe limits and no longer appeared likely to generate a tornado.The earlier tornado alert followed the detection of a severe storm near McArthur in Vinton County. Creola and Zaleski were among the communities that forecasters said could be affected as the storm moved east at about 24kmph.The flash-flood warning covered northeastern Vinton County, southwestern Athens County and northwestern Meigs County and was due to remain in effect until 6.30am Monday.Radar and automated gauges indicated that 6.4cm to 8.9cm of rain had already fallen, with another 2.5cm to 7.6cm possible.McArthur, Albany, Zaleski, Carpenter, Radcliffe and Creola were among the communities covered by the warning.The NWS advised people inside sturdy buildings to use a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor and stay away from windows. People outdoors, in vehicles or mobile homes were advised to seek substantial shelter, while drivers were warned not to enter flooded roads.This version removes the main repetition while keeping the latest-first structure, preserving the chronology and giving each subhead a clear factual purpose.
Article Summary: Severe thunderstorm warning issued for eastern vinton county and parts of southwestern athens, northwestern meigs, northeastern gallia and northeastern jackson counties. Radar indicated wind gusts of about 97kmph, while forecasters said a tornado remained possible.

Article Title: Australia ageing population crisis report sparks migration debate
Article Text:
People take photos of the Sydney Opera House in Sydney, Australia. (Photo: Reuters)

Older regions could face care-sector labour shortages

For the first time in the 2060s, deaths are projected to outnumber births in Australia, while annual population growth is expected to average 0.9% over the next four decades. Lower fertility and declining net overseas migration are expected to contribute to the slowdown, according to the Australian Treasury's 2026 Intergenerational Report released on Monday.That compares with average population growth of 1.4% a year over the previous four decades. Net overseas migration — migrant arrivals minus departures — is projected to decline further before levelling off.Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the number of Australians aged over 85 would triple by 2066, increasing demand for health services.Labor introduced tighter immigration rules last week amid rising support for One Nation, which has called for steep reductions in immigration. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's approval rating also fell to its lowest level since he took office in 2022, Reuters reported.For decades, migrant inflows have supported Australia's population growth despite persistently low birth rates. Japan, Germany and South Korea already record more deaths than births; Australia is projected to reach that point in the 2060s.Treasury's 40-year outlook is built around five major shifts: the artificial intelligence revolution, geopolitical fragmentation, the energy transition, aging and the care economy, and Australia's industrial transformation.Future budgets could include further tax cuts. The government has also been providing cost-of-living support as households contend with elevated inflation, mortgage costs and expensive housing.An older population is expected to require more care services. Staffing pressures are projected to be greater in regions with older populations, particularly in healthcare and aged care, where migrant workers form an important part of the workforce.
Article Summary: For the first time in the 2060s, deaths are projected to outnumber births in australia. Annual population growth is expected to average 0.9% over the next four decades. Lower fertility and declining net overseas migration are expected to contribute to the slowdown.

Article Title: Pakistan braces for protests as govt warns of $400 million daily loss
Article Text:
Protests in Pakistan (Representative image)

Government warns of economic fallout

Islamabad steps up security

Pakistan’s government has put heavy restrictions on protestors warning them that those seeking to march towards Islamabad with the government warning that disruptions could cost the economy around $400 million a day as separate marches by Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) put pressure on the capital.Pakistan’s information minister Attaullah Tarar said on Sunday that the administration, police and interior ministry were clear that groups intending to cause disruption would not be allowed to reach the capital. He cited a recent Islamabad high court ruling that bars political parties from obstructing public roads and the movement of citizens.The warning comes ahead of a PTI nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on September 27 seeking the release of party founder Imran Khan, who is incarcerated. JI, meanwhile, has launched a protest campaign against the petroleum levy and has begun a march towards the federal capital.Pakistan’s finance minister Muhammad Aurangzeb separately warned that strikes, sit-ins, long marches and road closures could cause an estimated PKR 120 billion (over $400 million) loss to Pakistan’s economy every day.According to estimates prepared by the planning commission and finance ministry, the services sector, including financial services, communication, retail, transport, wholesale and hospitality, could account for about PKR 86 billion of the daily loss.Industry could lose PKR 25 billion and agriculture PKR 9 billion, while the government could face an additional revenue loss of around PKR 17 billion.Aurangzeb said the disruption would come at a time when businesses were already dealing with higher freight and insurance costs and supply-chain problems linked to tensions in the Middle East, including disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab.He also warned about the impact on IT exports. Pakistan recorded $811 million in IT exports during July and August, he said, adding that previous internet disruptions during episodes of civil disobedience had affected IT exports by as much as 80%.Authorities have begun preparing for the potential marches, with hundreds of containers placed at entry points to Islamabad. Police officials have also reviewed security arrangements at major entry and exit points and other sensitive locations.The Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences and Federal Government Polyclinic Hospital have been placed on high alert, with emergency, trauma, ICU, operating theatre, blood bank and ambulance services instructed to remain fully operational. Pims said the arrangements would remain in place until September 30.The government has also cited concerns over statements by PTI leaders about the planned march. Pakistan’s parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said a reported remark by a senior PTI leader about turning Islamabad into “Somnath” had raised concerns about possible violence. He said the government had a responsibility to maintain law and order in the capital.The government has said it remains in contact with JI leadership and hopes to resolve the dispute through dialogue. JI has been protesting since August 16 against the petroleum levy and says it wants the government to withdraw the levy.
Article Summary: Jamaat-i-islami (ji) and imran khan’s pakistan tehreek- i-insaf (pti) put pressure on the capital. Ji has launched a protest campaign against the petroleum levy and has begun a march towards the federal capital. Government warns that strikes, sit-ins, long marches and road closures could cause an estimated pkr 120 billion (over $400 million) loss to pakistan's economy every day.

Article Title: US tells citizens to leave Iran immediately, warns of travel disruptions
Article Text:
US urges Americans to leave Iran

The United States has issued a fresh advisory against travel to Iran, urging American citizens to avoid the country “for any reason” and calling on those already there to leave immediately amid heightened tensions and the threat of further escalation in West Asia.In a security alert, the US Virtual Embassy in Iran said the regional security situation remained complex and cautioned that travellers could face flight cancellations, airspace closures and other disruptions.“Do not travel to Iran for any reason. US citizens should leave Iran now,” the advisory said.The US Mission urged Americans in the region to remain highly vigilant and closely monitor developments affecting airports, airlines and border crossings.It also warned that procedures at Iran’s land borders could change without notice and advised travellers to check the entry requirements of any country they may seek to enter.The US also cited the activities of Iranian-backed Houthi forces, which have carried out attacks in Saudi Arabia, including strikes targeting civilian airports.“Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports.This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly,” the alert said.The United States further warned that its diplomatic facilities, including locations outside the Middle East, have been targeted in the past and that Iran or groups supportive of Tehran could target US interests, businesses and institutions overseas.American citizens were advised to enrol in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security updates and facilitate contact with US diplomatic authorities during emergencies.The alert also urged citizens to avoid demonstrations, large gatherings and areas with a heavy police presence, while maintaining a low profile at locations publicly associated with the United States.In the event of an aerial attack, Americans were instructed to stay away from windows and glass doors, avoid fallen debris and monitor official communications.The alert comes amid an escalating confrontation between the United States and Iran, with Washington maintaining military and maritime pressure on Tehran and Iranian officials warning of retaliation against US interests in the region.The latest warning follows a separate US security alert for Americans and US government personnel in Saudi Arabia. The US Mission in Saudi Arabia recently required government employees to obtain special authorisation for official and personal travel to Taif and Yanbu amid heightened security concerns following Houthi attacks.Saudi authorities had also issued an emergency warning over a “hostile aerial threat” after a ballistic missile was launched towards Riyadh. Saudi-led coalition forces said the missile was intercepted and reported attempted attacks targeting civilians and infrastructure in Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu.
Article Summary: Us urges americans to leave iran for any reason. Travellers could face flight cancellations, airspace closures and other disruptions. Us also cited the activities of iranian-backed houthi forces, which have carried out attacks in saudi arabia. Alert comes amid an escalating confrontation between the united states and iran.

Article Title: Denver's historic bank building was bought for $17.6 million and got a $22.4 million renovation; after WeWork left, the 107,630-sq-ft property is now 100% vacant
Article Text:
The building was originally constructed in 1907 and was later redesigned by architects Fisher & Fisher (Photos: JLL Investor Center)

A historic building

The building also has a two-storey entrance with a 23-foot ceiling

The $22.4 million renovation

Could the bank become homes?

Eight of the building’s nine floors have been renovated and are ready for occupation

Newer buildings sold at steep discounts

Downtown's vacancy challenge

Denver’s historic bank building at 821 17th Street remains completely vacant despite a $22.4 million renovation after its owner bought the property for $17.6 million in 2017. The nine-storey building, now known as The Vault, has 107,630 square feet of office and retail space in the heart of downtown Denver’s former financial district.According to The Denver Gazette, the building was originally constructed in 1907 and was later redesigned by architects Fisher & Fisher. It was designated a Denver Landmark in 1977. The property was one of the financial buildings that once formed the 'Wall Street of the Rockies', when the area around 17th, Champa and Stout streets was a major centre of Denver’s commercial activity.Harbor Associates, based in Seal Beach, California, bought the building in 2017. The owner later invested more than $22.4 million in improvements, including a new lobby, restoration of the first and second floors, exterior facade work and upgrades to the building’s mechanical systems. JLL is now presenting the property for sale as an opportunity for office use, adaptive reuse or conversion into residential or hospitality space.Finding tenants has proved difficult, however. WeWork leased about 40,000 square feet of the building in 2018 but left in 2021 as the pandemic changed office-working patterns.The Vault’s current situation reflects a much wider change in Upper Downtown Denver. Office vacancies across downtown have remained high, although they have dipped slightly to around 38%, according to The Denver Gazette. Some newer office properties have also been sold at heavily reduced prices, with buyers considering residential conversions as one possible way to reuse the space.The area around The Vault once went through another major transformation. Downtown Denver’s historic commercial districts had struggled during the 1960s, when older buildings deteriorated and businesses moved away. By the 1980s and 1990s, however, parts of downtown were becoming active again as Denver developed into a sports and entertainment centre.The former bank building itself became part of that revival. Its large basement vault became the centrepiece of the Broker Restaurant, which opened in 1972 and remained there until it closed permanently in 2017. In 1978, the building also became home to Women’s Bank, which was widely recognised for its focus on women-owned businesses and lending to women.JLL’s property listing describes The Vault as a 'fully repositioned' 107,630-square-foot office and retail landmark. It says eight of the building’s nine floors have been renovated and are ready for occupation, with furnished office suites.The listing says the property is being offered without existing leases. That gives a potential buyer the option to continue with office use or use it for residential or hospitality conversion.The building also has a two-storey entrance with a 23-foot ceiling. JLL describes the atrium as a major feature of the property. The listing also highlights restored historic details, including stained-glass skylights, hand-painted ceiling beams and a sculpted mezzanine frieze.However, The Denver Gazette also reported that a view through the locked doors of the main floor showed areas that appeared to need additional finish work.The possibility of converting The Vault into residential space is being considered as downtown Denver looks for ways to reduce its large amount of unused office space.Bill Mosher, a former chief project officer for the Denver Downtown Development Authority, said historic buildings can have advantages when they are converted.“Generally, historic buildings have real possibilities,” Mosher told The Denver Gazette. “They have lobbies that are interesting spaces.”The Vault has an L-shaped design, with the two wings measuring about 50 feet wide. That layout could provide window access and floor plans that may work for apartments, according to the report. The building is also much smaller in scale than some newer downtown office towers.However, architect-engineer Bradley L. Zieg said converting an office building into homes is not simple because the two types of buildings are designed differently.“Most buildings of any kind of stature were designed and built to a specific use,” Zieg told The Denver Gazette. “Converting offices into residential uses is a real stretch. Residential architecture is fundamentally different than whatever else you would do,” he said.Zieg also pointed to problems involving heating, cooling, ventilation and plumbing. “Even if you can solve the space-planning problem, now you’ve got all the plumbing. You’ve got all the provided heat and cooling. It’s a nightmare.”The challenge for The Vault is that some newer downtown properties have changed hands at much lower prices. Former Los Angeles mayoral candidate Asher Luzzatto has bought four buildings covering a combined 1.75 million square feet.Those purchases included the Denver Energy Center, which was reportedly bought for $5.25 million after having sold for $176 million a decade earlier.Mosher said the low purchase prices make such conversions easier to consider. “The reason Luzzatto is doing those is that he bought them for less than 10 bucks a foot,” Mosher said. “It’s hard to do that with $29 million sunk into building.”Greg Paugh, vice president and broker at Stream Realty Partners, said The Vault reflects the wider uncertainty facing downtown Denver.“For several institutional owners that have been trying to hold strong, they’ve decided it’s time to cut bait and for the few playing the long game, betting on Denver’s recovery, it’s another opportunity to capitalise on another heavily discounted sale,” Paugh said.Paugh said demand may be shifting from LoDo towards areas farther east of Larimer Street. He also said some tenants were moving from Cherry Creek and the Denver Tech Center.“The Vault sits firmly in the CBD, and this may help downtown’s perception if it truly can be revitalised,” Paugh said.He added that he did not expect the historic building to sell at the single-digit prices seen for some newer towers. But he said “it will not be in the first wave of downtown comebacks.”
Article Summary: The nine-storey building, now known as the vault, has 107,630 square feet of office and retail space in the heart of downtown denver’s former financial district. It was originally constructed in 1907 and was later redesigned by architects fisher & fisher.
